Synopsis:
    Canada shed 41,700 jobs in August, badly missing the +15,000 consensus, with losses concentrated in full-time positions and service sectors. Unemployment held at 6.4% (a two-year low), partly due to labor force contraction from tighter immigration and aging demographics. Wage growth slumped to a 7-year low of 2%. Critically, this is the last data print before Trump's new 50% tariffs and Canadian retaliation kick in next week, raising the near-term risk of trade-exposed sector layoffs accelerating. The underlying labor market momentum is now broadly seen as stalling.
